growth_story.headline: Algeria's income per person grew 3.1 percent a year in 1998–2005, then only 0.7 for two decades still tied to oil and gas; it reached a new high in 2025.
growth_story.arc: Algeria's income per person fell by 1.3 percent a year on average from 1990 to 1997, in the years after the 1986 oil price crash and during a decade of civil strife. From 1998 to 2005 it grew by 3.1 percent a year: an IMF-supported adjustment had tightened public finances, stability returned by the end of the 1990s, and oil and gas output and prices rose. Since 2006 growth has averaged only 0.7 percent a year. It ran at 1.0 in 2006–2015, when the oil windfall paid for heavy public spending, and at 0.5 in 2016–2025, after oil prices fell in 2014 and the pandemic and an oil shock struck together in 2020. A recovery since 2021, which the sources link to public investment and to growth outside oil and gas, took income per person to its highest level yet in 2025.

growth_story.tension: The sources call recent growth robust and investment strong, and investment is high at 35.8 percent of GDP, well above what Algeria's income would predict. Yet income per person grew only 0.5 percent a year over 2016–2025. In 2024 it was only back to about its 2016 level, because the losses from 2017 to 2020 were large and the economy's growth is shared among a growing population.
